title: The $4-Per-Serving Creamy Tuscan Chicken That Beats My Local Italian Spot
description: Skip the $25 takeout. This creamy tuscan chicken uses Aldi staples and one pan for a 20-minute dinner that is way cheaper and better than a restaurant.
story: Honestly, after a soul-crushing Tuesday at work, the last thing I wanted to do was drop $30 on DoorDash for soggy pasta. I looked at my tiny apartment kitchen and realized I had a pack of chicken breasts from my Sunday Aldi run and that jar of sun-dried tomatoes I bought at Trader Joe's months ago. This creamy tuscan chicken is my absolute go-to when I need to feel fancy on a budget. The first time I tested this, I cranked the skillet too high and totally burnt the garlic—it tasted bitter and ruined the whole sauce. Lesson learned: keep the heat medium-low for that golden aroma! Now, this meal costs me about $4 per serving instead of the $25 I'd pay downtown. It’s rich, garlicky, and only uses one pan, which means I’m not scrubbing dishes until midnight. It's the ultimate win for my bank account and my sanity.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken breast, sliced into thin cutlets
1 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half for a lighter swap)
instructions: Step 1: Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Season the chicken with salt and sear until golden brown on both sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside on a plate.

Step 2: In the same pan, drop the heat to medium-low. Add the minced garlic and sun-dried tomatoes. Sauté for about 1 minute until the kitchen smells incredible, but watch that garlic so it doesn't get too dark.
Step 3: Pour in the heavy cream and bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the Parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes until the sauce starts to thicken up and look velvety.
Step 4: Toss in the spinach until it wilts, then slide the chicken back into the pan. Let it bubble for 2 more minutes so the chicken soaks up the cream and everything is heated through.
proHack: To get that restaurant-style thickness without using a flour roux, let the cream simmer and reduce for an extra 3 minutes before adding the cheese. It concentrates the flavor and makes the sauce cling to the chicken perfectly.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. When reheating, add a splash of milk or water before microwaving to loosen the sauce back up, as creamy sauces tend to tighten up when cold.

faqs.question: Can I use milk instead of heavy cream?
faqs.answer: You can use whole milk, but the sauce will be thinner. I suggest whisking in 1 teaspoon of cornstarch to the cold milk first to help it thicken up without curdling.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the sauce from separating?
faqs.answer: Keep your heat on a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. High heat can make the dairy break and look grainy; low and slow is the secret for a smooth sauce.
